title: Ireland – Education and training services – Online learning expertise and scientific advisory (UCC-VEAT-2024-02)
description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. This notice acknowledges that University College Cork contracted with Randbee Consultants SRL, for the provision of support and leadership of online learning resource maintenance, development and enhancement for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Randbee Consultants SL will lead the online learning resource activities for the overall Service contract, provide technical support to implement resource solutions, contribute niche expertise to the Scientific Advisory Committee, and support Training event implementation and online content maintenance services. Randbee Consultants SRL were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform their role in this overall service contract, further enhanced by their good standing, and track record of excellence. They have an extensive track record of working with European and International projects, providing valuable services and training on Copernicus product applications, Earth Observation, Geographical Information Systems (GIS), statistical analysis, modelling, and web visualization tools. The company's experience with both in-person and remote training formats aligns strongly with the diverse delivery methods outlined in the overarching Service Contract. They also have experience with working for the ECMWF, and within their staff had the required expertise in satellite data, end-user applications, and teaching and learning, to contribute to the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – and highly beneficial professional networks. For example, their experience in successfully delivered training on Copernicus data and services in Ecuador, and in hosting online seminars, workshops, and Copernicus hackathons in various locations (e.g. Oman, Spain), demonstrated their adaptability and reach. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completed it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

title: Ireland – Installation services of fire protection equipment – Tender for the Design, Supply and Installation of Fire Extinguishing (Suppression) Systems in 3 MCC Rooms at MEDITE Europe DAC ‘26
description: MEDITE Europe DAC are looking for suitably qualified Fire suppression companies to install suppression systems in the following Motor Control Centre (MCC) rooms across the Medite plant. • Anner HV Sub-Station • Fire-Pump House MCC • Line1 post-press MCC Project Background Mandatory Insurance Requirement Medite electrical distribution network comprises 17 Motor Control Centre rooms, and the main HV Switch-room located at Anner Substation. (See MCC layout drawing in Appendix 3). A number of these MCCs and the main Switch-room are considered higher impact and risk, due to the criticality of the processes they support and the ageing condition of the installed switchgear and associated cooling systems. Overall Program Objectives The multi-year goal of this program is to ensure that all site MCC + HV switch-room comply with legislative requirements and industry best practice for extinguishing electrical fires automatically. It is proposed to install a similar Clean Agent gaseous suppression system with appropriate smoke detection in all MCC rooms, starting with those with critical switchgear. Program estimated to take ~4 years. The program scope includes: • Design of suppression system for each room considering:  Size and fabric of structure  Presence of a floor void(s) or not  Age + condition of switchgear (risk of overheating + fire)  Ability to seal room effectively *  Type of cooling + air-handling (AHU) in place  Characterization of pressure in room now – Positive or Negative **  Ability to locate pressurized cylinders nearby • All necessary civil, mechanical and electrical (pre)works to enable the chosen system(s) • Integration of each system’s controls into the existing plant fire alarm system, where applicable to deliver the project goals • Ensure compatibility of control system with existing ones (fire control panel) * for total flood systems ** most Medite MCCs are positive pressure to keep out dust As part of the 2026 program of works the following 3 electrical rooms are to be addressed: • Anner Sub-station switch-room • Fire Pumphouse MCC room • Line1 Press Outfeed MCC room Preferred route is to install an Inert Gas system with appropriate Smoke Detection system. Scope of Works • Evaluate Enclosure Integrity Test results (‘door-fan’ test report) • Determine existing baseline for cooling, air-handling + room pressure profile • Based on results of EIT report referenced in Appendix 3, recommend and execute remedial measures • Determine and design optimal suppression system • Design and specify all necessary smoke / heat detection systems • Fire seal room to appropriate fire-rate • Install fire detection system • Install suppression system • Link system to house alarm and test • Validate and certify finished system *** Please see the attached Tender Document for the full and Complete scope of Works ***

title: TGO-MEX RADIO OCCULTATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: RO occurs when the transmitter of a radio signal appears to set behind a planet, as viewed from a receiving station. The radio signal is refracted by the atmosphere and ionosphere causing a frequency shift; analysing this frequency shift allows reconstruction of a high-resolution vertical profile of density (and thus pressure and temperature) in the neutral atmosphere and ionospheric electronabundances in the ionosphere. Spacecraft-to-Earth RO has been carried out for many decades by planetary missions, but the opportunities for this are limited by the orbital geometry and ground station availability.

title: Connectiviteit FIFA WK 2026
description: Van 11 juni 2026 tot 19 juli 2026 vindt het eindtoernooi van de FIFA WK Voetbal 2026 plaats in Canada, Mexico en de USA. Voor dit evenement bundelen VRT, RTBF en NOS hun krachten om de connectiviteit van broadcast video, audio en data te organiseren tussen hun thuiskantoren en het International Broadcast Centre in Dallas, USA meer bepaald het Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center. Deze procedure beschrijft de basisbehoeften aan diensten voor deze connectiviteit. De inschrijver is verantwoordelijk voor het toevoegen van alles wat nodig is om een betrouwbare en rotsvaste oplossing voor deze operatie te krijgen. FIFA beperkt de leveranciers die lijnen in de IBC-faciliteit kunnen brengen. De geselecteerde partner is Telstra/Vidi. RTBF| NOS| VRT heeft 2 onafhankelijke 10Gbps lijnen bestellen tussen de IBC en een POP-locatie naar keuze.(DALLAS 01 & DALLAS 09 - zie bijlage communicatie FIFA/Telstra/Vidi) De aannemer is verantwoordelijk voor het opvangen van de signalen in deze POP's en deze naar de thuiskantoren van RTBF/VRT in Brussel, België en NOS in Hilversum, Nederland te brengen. Alle 3 broadcaster moeten bereikt worden via een onafhankelijk en redundante pad (creatie Blue & Red Circuit) vanuit Dalles via beide POP's naar de broadcasters. De technische apparatuur van de aannemer kan worden geplaatst in het IBC-kantoor van NOS/RTBF/VRT dat met een 12-core dark fiber wordt verbonden met de Third Party Telco-ruimte. De signalen zullen in Dallas aangeleverd worden in 1080p/60 en moeten door de aanbieder geconverteerd worden naar de respectievelijke huisstandaard van NOS (1080p/50) en VRT en RTBF (1080i/50), muv eventuele specifieke signalen. title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF A DEPLOYER FOR STACKED SMALL SATCOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.035) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of the in-orbit experiment is to conduct an experiment and develop the ability of a stack of small satellites to be deployed from a launch vehicle. The activity will design and build a launch vehicle adapter, satellite deployer and compatible test satellite/s which will be subjected to an on ground and in-orbit experiment test campaign examining the deployment dynamics from a launch vehicle in microgravity conditions and subsequent orbit behaviour of the launch vehicle upper stage and test satellites.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source for small satellite deployers for stacked satellites within the launch vehicle fairing, allowing for 50% increase in utilisation of the launchvolume compared to the current state of art.Description: Current satellite deployment approaches which integrate satellites on a vertical satellite payload adapter structure within a launcher fairing underutilise the available volume, limiting the number of small satellites that can be launched per mission. Stacked satellite integration could increase volume and mass utilisation by up to 50% for a given launch increasingthe number of satellites deployed per mission, reducing mission capex and reducing time to deploy an operational constellation. However, there are no European solutions currently in use for deploying multiple small satellites in a stacked configuration. A Small Satellite Design Guideline (SSGL) has recently been developed that provides design guidelines forplatform developers which allow for the horizontal and vertical stacking of multiple satellites in medium and heavy lift launch vehicles. This concept has carried out critical technology derisking through on-ground tests and simulations.This activity will make use of the SSGL and the activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1, with a budget of up to 4 MEuro, will design and develop the Stack Deployment Mechanism and LV adapter, Test Satellites and validate their mechanical and deployment performance in ground-based environments and simulations preparing it forthe in-orbit experiment. Deliverables from Phase 1 are Study Report and Full Engineering Models of the deployer and test satellites.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the satellites. The structural performance of the stack will be monitored through the launch phase. The deployment performance will be investigated through satellite GNSS and attitude data, as well asrelative position and poise estimation from sensors based on the launch vehicle adapter. Data generated in this phase help to increase the precision of mathematical models and digital twins used for solving satellite motion during deployment and orbital mechanicsverification required to refine the SSGL. Deliverables from Phase 1 are summary report and flight engineering models of the deployer and test satellites.
